content:
After months of testing, macOS 27 Golden Gate is now officially rolling out to all users, bringing an all-new Siri AI, deeper Liquid Glass refinements, several major new Safari features, and a series of performance and user experience improvements. Here's everything you need to know about this update.

At this year's WWDC, Apple took a slightly different approach to introducing their operating systems.

Instead of covering each platform one by one, Apple reduced the time spent on individual operating systems and shifted the focus to cross-platform features and improvements—mainly because many features rely on the new Apple Intelligence framework.

However, macOS 27 Golden Gate still includes plenty of thoughtful design and feature refinements, starting with several Liquid Glass adjustments.

Liquid Glass and Interface Improvements

Although macOS Tahoe 26 adopted Apple's new design language, it still lagged visually—especially compared to iOS 26 and iPadOS 26.

In macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple spent more time further integrating the new Liquid Glass throughout the system, while also introducing some visual adjustments from iOS 27 and iPadOS 27—including a new Liquid Glass slider that lets users adjust the transparency effect themselves.

There's a fun easter egg hidden in the Liquid Glass appearance settings: Clarus the Dogcow—just scroll the demo panel all the way down and you'll find it.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also redesigned app icons to better match the Liquid Glass design, by adding an extra layer to bring depth and detail to the global system appearance across light, dark, tinted, and transparent looks.

The red, yellow, and green traffic light buttons introduced mid-beta have also been updated. The previously flat green, yellow, and red controls now sport Liquid Glass styling, and feature a delightful bounce effect when users click (or briefly tap?) and drag before releasing.

Another thoughtful interface improvement in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Apple's decision to unify the corner radius of windows and apps across the entire system, rather than dynamically adjusting based on UI elements in the window's menu bar.

Although Apple's choice was intentional, many people thought the inconsistent corner radius was a bug—prompting Apple to specifically mention this change during the WWDC keynote.

Another controversial design decision involves icons. macOS 26 Tahoe added a symbol next to almost every menu command, intended to make menus easier to scan, but it was widely criticized for making the interface more cluttered, and in some cases actually harder to scan.

Fortunately in macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple has changed course, removing most of these icons and returning menus to a cleaner, more streamlined appearance.

Other visual refinements in macOS 27 Golden Gate include edge-to-edge sidebars and clearer differentiation of the currently active window—both of which were controversial during macOS Tahoe 26.

Siri AI and the New Siri App

This could arguably be the most important new feature of macOS 27 Golden Gate. The new Siri was co-developed with Google's Gemini model, has its own dedicated app, and is deeply integrated into the system.

The new Siri AI uses a new on-device indexing system to handle user data, and exists simultaneously in Spotlight and the new Siri app.

The new Siri app looks and operates similarly to other AI assistant apps: a conversation history list on the left spanning compatible platforms, and a main chat panel in the center where you can type prompts, attach images or files, or start a conversation with your voice. The app also supports search and pinned conversations—a plus for users with different workflows.

The new Siri AI can pull information from the web and the user's personal data to provide actionable answers. During testing, the response to the new Siri was mostly positive, though it was occasionally slightly slower than other LLM-based AI assistants users expected.

Another practical feature of the new Siri AI is that it can interact with native and third-party apps and perform actions directly—a major improvement over the old Siri's app integration capabilities.

Developers need to expose their app's content and functionality through the App Intents framework, so as more developers update their apps for macOS 27 Golden Gate, this aspect is expected to keep improving.

Finally, the system also adds a universal "Ask Siri" context menu option, allowing users to select text, images, or files and then query Siri directly. For example, you can Control-click on an image in a document to ask Siri for more information; or select a passage of text and ask Siri to rewrite, proofread, adjust the tone, or provide writing suggestions.

Siri AI launches supporting English, with French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish being added in October. Due to regulatory reasons, Siri AI is currently unavailable in China and the EU.

Apple Intelligence

We've previously covered Apple's new foundation models in detail. To put it simply, in its 2027 OS release, Apple developed a new generation of Apple Intelligence models. Here are Apple's official descriptions for each model:

AFM 3 Core, the next generation of our 3-billion parameter dense model, with further quality improvements. AFM 3 Core Advanced, our most powerful on-device model, with native support for multimodality, more expressive speech, and more accurate dictation. This 20-billion parameter model is built on Apple's cutting-edge research and uses a sparse architecture, activating only 1 to 4 billion parameters on demand. AFM 3 Core Advanced requires and has been optimized for our most powerful Apple Silicon systems. AFM 3 Cloud, our server-side workhorse model, designed for speed, efficiency, and capability. ADM 3 Cloud (Image), for image generation and editing, unlocking more advanced photo editing tools, the new Image Playground, and more. AFM 3 Cloud Pro, our most powerful server-side model, powering the most demanding use cases, such as agentic tool use and complex reasoning.

In practice, macOS 27 Golden Gate uses two on-device models—AFM 3 Core and AFM 3 Core Advanced—with the rest running in the cloud. The performance of these two on-device models depends on the Mac's hardware, particularly available memory, to handle their activated parameters and other AI workloads.

As for Apple Intelligence's real-world performance on macOS 27 Golden Gate, it's a mixed bag. The models themselves perform quite well on everyday tasks—such as helping draft emails, proofreading documents, or summarizing content.

The issue is that Apple sometimes now seems overly enthusiastic about how and when to present Siri AI—sometimes annoying users, or even getting in the way of what they're trying to do.

One standout new Apple Intelligence feature in macOS 27 Golden Gate is the new Visual Intelligence shortcut. Simply press Command-Shift-S Space to select any area on screen and instantly query Siri—whether it's an image, PDF, text, or just about anything displayed on screen.

Unfortunately, not all Macs compatible with macOS 27 can run the new Apple Intelligence—this feature requires an A18 Pro, M1, or later chip. Here is the official list of Mac models Apple has published as supporting the new features:

  • MacBook Neo (2026)
  • MacBook Air with Apple Silicon (2020 or later)
  • MacBook Pro with Apple Silicon (2020 or later)
  • iMac with Apple Silicon (2021 or later)
  • Mac mini with Apple Silicon (2020 or later)
  • Mac Studio (2022 or later)
  • Mac Pro with Apple Silicon (2023)

Most Apple Intelligence features support languages where Apple Intelligence is already available, including Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Danish, Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

Due to regulatory reasons, Apple Intelligence is currently unavailable in China. Apple also notes that some Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features will have usage restrictions, though the company has not yet announced specific details.

Performance and Stability Improvements

During the WWDC26 keynote, Apple highlighted dozens of improvements across all operating systems.

For macOS 27 Golden Gate, these include faster AirDrop transfers, improved network file browsing, faster Spotlight indexing (especially for shortcuts and actions), and faster iCloud Photos uploads with selective priority sync.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also improves scrolling performance in Safari and Calendar, as well as animation performance in Mission Control and Spaces. Apple also tweaked Mail indexing and search, and the underlying system for Spotlight suggestions.

Other improvements include more consistent and persistent window position memory on external displays, HDR support for system UI elements, broader support for high-resolution and high-refresh-rate modes on external displays, and improved Sidecar touch support—including tap controls, single-finger scrolling, system gestures, and markup features.

Safari

macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces a Safari feature called "Notify Me" that can monitor web pages and notify users when relevant changes occur—such as price drops, restocks, event registration openings, or anything else users want to track.

Notify Me can check hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly, and you can also specify additional days and times for checks.

In addition, Safari in macOS 27 Golden Gate adds a "Describe an Extension" feature that lets users create extensions using natural language.

To help users get started, Apple provides several examples covering productivity, focus, creative, and design/development areas. Users can also simply describe what they need in their own words and let Apple Intelligence handle the rest.

Both of these features can be accessed from the "More Options" hamburger menu on the right side of existing tabs.

For users who love keeping tons of tabs open, Safari can now automatically organize and group tabs by topic.

Another thoughtful touch in Safari for macOS 27 Golden Gate is the addition of a pull-to-refresh gesture similar to iOS and iPadOS, where users can swipe down through a "rubber band" effect to refresh the page.

This gesture also applies to other system apps, such as Mail, News, and Calendar; many see this as a further hint at the rumored touchscreen Mac, which might be announced as early as this year.

iPhone Mirroring

With macOS 27 Golden Gate, users can now resize the iPhone Mirroring window to different aspect ratios; many see this as an early sign of Apple paving the way for a foldable iPhone.

With iPhone Duo now officially available, Mac users can be the first to experience this. Unfortunately, Apple notes that iPhone Mirroring is still unavailable in the EU.

Shortcuts

This is arguably one of the most practical new Apple Intelligence features in this year's OS updates.

Although Shortcuts itself is already a fairly approachable automation tool, it can still be daunting for general users. Now home users only need to describe what they want to do, and Apple Intelligence will build it into a native Shortcut.

To help users get started, the Shortcuts app also highlights several suggestions on the new shortcut creation screen, including:

  • Dictate and translate into Spanish
  • Write a haiku for the weather forecast
  • Play my workout playlist whenever I arrive at the gym
  • Make a recipe with these leftovers
  • Summarize my day every morning
  • Prioritize my to-do list every morning
  • Get driving directions as soon as I get in the car
  • Dictate my thoughts and save them to the clipboard
  • Dim the screen when it's bedtime
  • Turn on Do Not Disturb when opening the TV app

By the way, if you want to dive deeper into Shortcuts, remember to follow Stephen Robles on YouTube and Instagram. You can also check out Shortcuts Playground on MacStories, a more powerful natural language shortcut builder.

Photos

The Photos app now offers three editing tools powered by Apple Intelligence: an enhanced Clean Up tool that can remove objects, people, or other unwanted elements from photos; Extend, which can generate surrounding areas when you feel the original was cropped too tightly; and Spatial Recompose, which lets you change the angle and composition of a photo after it's taken.

In addition, iCloud Shared Albums now support full-resolution sharing and can invite Windows and Android users to join via iCloud.com.

Other new features include being able to play any set of photos and videos as a slideshow with custom music, transitions, and playback duration, a photo rating feature with a new star-rating system, and a brand-new dedicated "Shot by Me" collection.

More macOS 27 Golden Gate Details

  • Calendar lets users add, edit, or update events by describing them.
  • Finder can now intelligently suggest names for files and folders based on their contents.
  • Image Playground has expanded support for different styles and uses a new foundation model for better results.
  • Maps' Flyover experience has been upgraded, delivering better textures, detail, and clarity for hundreds of cities worldwide.
  • Messages finally (finally) integrates tap-back reaction notifications and improves cross-device sync performance.
  • Notes supports handwriting and drawing with the trackpad, expanded Markdown support, and adds copy/paste and Section Links features.
  • Podcasts now supports video podcasts and comes with picture-in-picture playback.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also marks the final version to support Rosetta. As Apple explains, "Only apps that have not been updated since installing this update will be unable to run on Macs with Apple Silicon"—you can learn more here.

Compatibility

According to Apple's official list, macOS 27 Golden Gate is compatible with the following Mac models:

  • MacBook Neo (2026)

What's your favorite new feature? Let us know in the comments.
